title: Ratan Prakash v. State of Uttar Pradesh
coram: Arindam Sinha, J.; Dr. Yogendra Kumar Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; no interference, cl. 6.5 available and bill undisclosed.
headnote: Correction of an electricity bill is not entertained in writ where the bill is not disclosed. Grievance redressal for an incorrect bill is under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Ratan Prakash sought a writ for correction and re-calculation of an electricity bill dated 11 November 2024. The bill itself was not placed on the record. Counsel for the supply company submitted that the petition was not maintainable because it had not been filed by the consumer, the petitioner's wife. Additional Chief Standing Counsel appeared for the State. The Division Bench disposed of the writ without examining the bill.

holding_units.holding: Grievance redressal for an incorrect electricity bill is provided in clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where the petitioner has not disclosed the allegedly incorrect bill, the High Court is not called upon to interfere in writ jurisdiction.

not_decided.point: Whether the writ is maintainable when filed by the consumer's husband rather than the consumer herself
not_decided.note: Licensee objected that the consumer was the petitioner's wife; the Court did not rule on locus.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the bill dated 11 November 2024
not_decided.note: The bill was not disclosed; no merits examination.
